newsitem.title: USA: Whirlpool earnings jump 25 pct despite lower sales.
newsitem.headline: Whirlpool earnings jump 25 pct despite lower sales.

text.p: Whirlpool Corp. said Tuesday its earnings jumped 25 percent in the second quarter, as the world's largest maker of home appliances shrugged off a drop in sales.
The company earned $65 million, or 86 cents a share, vs. year-ago profits of $52 million, or 70 cents a share.

Sales, however, fell 7 percent to $2.1 billion from $2.2 billion, which the Benton Harbour, Mich.-based firm attributed to weak air conditioner shipments in North America and the effect of the strong dollar on currency translations from its European operations.

"Our performance this quarter has been led by significant improvements in our European business, due primarily to our ability to manage costs in a tough economic environment, while strengthening our product mix and improving our margins," said Chief Executive Officer David Whitwam.
"The North and Latin American businesses continued their solid performance, while Asia's results reflect the ongoing challenges of building Whirlpool's presence in that region," he said.
North American second-quarter unit shipments were flat with last year's record levels, Whirlpool said.
In Europe, shipments improved slightly and sales rose 2.5 percent in local currency terms but were down 6.7 percent when translated to U.S. dollars.
Latin American sales were up nearly 8 percent vs. a year earlier, while Whirlpool Asia had a operating loss relating to the costs of developing a Chinese joint venture, the company said.
Whirlpool's stock was off 19 cents at $52.44 on the New York Stock Exchange.
